name: Shenandoah beard

image.caption: Amish Man in straw hat, suspenders, and shenandoah beard

lead: The Shenandoah is a beard in which hair is grown full and long along the jaw and chin, joining the sideburns, while the area above the mouth is shaved.

For looks, it frames the jawline and lower face and can add visual length to the chin, while leaving the upper lip clean. It is known as an Amish beard and, in the Lincoln form, is associated with Abraham Lincoln.

paras: The style is grown out along the jaw and chin and the moustache area is kept shaved, with the beard kept trimmed to a chosen length and shape.
No health risks are specific to the style; shaving and trimming carry ordinary skin irritation risks. It carries religious or cultural associations for some groups.

angle.text: The beard accentuates the jaw outline and chin. Wearers use it to add definition around the lower face.

lead: A Shenandoah is a beard style in which hair is grown full and long over the jaw and chin, joining the sideburns, while the hair above the mouth is shaved [1]. It is also called an Amish beard, chin curtain, Donegal, Dutch beard, Lincoln, spade beard or whaler [1].

The style is common among married Amish men, who generally grow a beard after baptism but shave the moustache, and is popular among some Salafi Sunni Muslims [1]. Wikipedia lists Abraham Lincoln among notable wearers [1].
For appearance, the style outlines the jaw and chin and leaves the upper lip clean, giving a different frame to the face from full beards or goatees.

paras: The beard joins the sideburns, covers the jaw and chin, and omits the moustache [1]. Wikipedia notes use by Amish men after marriage and by some Salafi Sunnis, with Lincoln, Edward Bates and Charles Taze Russell among those shown wearing it [1][2].
